title: Rule
description: The frontmatter of rules/<context-slug>/<rule-slug>.md (SPEC-003). Three subtypes, each changing validation: an invariant constrains inside one aggregate and holds immediately; a policy may cross aggregates or contexts and then declares consistency — immediate across an aggregate boundary is a validation error; a state-machine anchors to one aggregate root and its status enumeration, and the validator checks totality over its transition set. A rule carries no examples: a concrete case is a Scenario anchored to the rule. The body carries `## Description`.

expression.description: The rule stated so a consumer can evaluate it.

constrains.description: The Domain Model elements this rule binds, by full identity.

consistency.description: How a policy holds. Required where constrains crosses an aggregate or context boundary, and it must be eventual there: an immediate demand across a boundary is a boundary redrawn, not a rule.

subject.description: State-machine only: the aggregate root whose states this governs. At most one state-machine per subject.

status.description: State-machine only: the enumeration whose values are the states.

terminal.description: States that accept no further trigger; exempt from the totality check because declared.

rejections.description: Decided non-transitions. Every pairing of a non-terminal state with a mentioned trigger is a transition or a rejection; an undecided pairing is a decision to make and log, never silence.

examples.statement: A hypothesis MUST hold at least one piece of evidence before its case resolves.
An alert unresolved for 24 hours MUST open a case.
A case moves only along the declared transitions.
examples.subject: domain/troubleshooting/case

domainRef.description: A Domain Model element, by full identity — rules sit in their own directory, so no reference is bare.
